Good morning! Here's the latest in trending:AI strength: AMD pops on earnings beat; records $1B charge tied to warrants. U.S. concerns: Oracle (ORCL) scraps $7B AI chip lease with Tencent (TCEHY).Split in two: CVS (CVS) plans to separate its pharmacy and insurance businesses.

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 AI strength: AMD  pops on earnings beat ; records $1B charge tied to warrants . 

 U.S. concerns: Oracle ( ORCL ) scraps $7B AI chip lease with Tencent ( TCEHY ).

 Split in two: CVS ( CVS ) plans to separate its pharmacy and insurance businesses.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Flip the script 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
The Democratic Party has swept the U.S. midterm ​elections, winning control of both the Senate and the House, significantly reshaping Trump's final two years in office. The Democratic majority will take over in January, raising the odds of legislative gridlock, tougher corporate oversight, increased pushback on the U.S.-Iran war and probes into  possible corruption .

 More scrutiny: Any legislation to rein in the AI buildout at the federal level will likely fail due to Trump's veto power. But Democrats have now secured a majority of governorships, meaning they could bring in more hurdles for data center plans in key states. For example, incoming Texas Governor Gina Hinojosa has called for a moratorium on new data center projects until protections are established for electricity supplies, water resources, and local communities. "Given much of U.S. growth currently relies on the AI boom, stricter policy could start forming a headwind," ING strategists cautioned. "Probably not something that will materialize in big changes in the near term, but definitely a trend to keep an eye on." "At the very least, data center builders are likely to have to offer more incentives to local communities," UBS' Paul Donovan said.  AI stocks tied to Texas data center in focus 

 Dig deeper: Companies that granted stakes to the U.S. government could face scrutiny, such as Intel ( INTC ) and MP Materials ( MP ). That scrutiny could extend to corporate donors that spent record sums this midterm cycle, such as Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCE ) CEO Elon Musk . Donors for Trump's ballroom project could also be put under the scanner, including Meta ( META ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Apple ( AAPL ). Meanwhile, the renewable energy sector that has faltered under the Trump administration could see a resurgence. Solar stocks are rallying today as Democrats' midterm wins could translate to stronger support for renewable energy policies . Recall that the last Democratic-controlled Congress passed the Inflation Reduction Act in 2022, which included tax credits for renewable energy, nuclear power and EVs.

 Fiscal outlook: There's a higher risk of fiscal gridlock from next year, at a time when the national debt is past $40T. Congress will likely find it harder to agree on new spending, which could bring about a government shutdown. "Bonds are coming out as the clear winner as markets put the AI trade on the chopping block ​and embrace the higher ⁠possibility that further tax cuts are put on ice and government spending slows," Prashant Newnaha, senior rates strategist at TD Securities, told Reuters . What about the inflation outlook? "With Trump still in charge of foreign policy, inflation remains a bit of a wild card ," ING noted. "The war with Iran is not over, and oil barely budged on the election results. Tariffs could make a return as one of Trump’s favorite policy measures." There's also the possibility of the Democrat-controlled Senate blocking Trump's nominees for future vacant roles, such as in the Supreme ​Court and the Federal Reserve. (4 comments)

Anthropic ( ANT ) 'gobbling up' compute capacity ahead of IPO .

Borrowing spree: Meta ( META ) launches debut euro bond sale .

Google ( GOOGL ) extends voluntary buyouts to more countries .

Boeing ( BA ) sees Middle East aircraft fleet doubling by 2045 .
